reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about segregation, brittle phase nucleation, and toughness reduction in high-entropy alloys, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises.
premises: Thermally induced elemental segregation occurs at grain boundaries in high-entropy alloys.
This segregation nucleates brittle phases at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary embrittlement from segregation/brittle phases reduces toughness.
Toughness loss correlates with aging time due to increased segregation.
